The same design process and technical communication can organize many fabrication methods. Select a process because it suits the part, material, quantity, finish, and evidence required by the design.

## Additional methods

- vinyl cutting and applied graphics;
- plasma cutting and thermal-cutting workflows;
- sheet-metal layout, cutting, bending, and fastening;
- vacuum forming and mold design;
- molding and casting;
- composite layup and finishing;
- hybrid projects that choose several processes for different functions.

Each method should begin with the N.I.C.E. design process, explain what the process is suited to, distinguish digital geometry from machine setup, and require testing rather than presenting generic settings as universal.

## Free cross-process resources

Study documented builds on [Instructables](https://www.instructables.com/) and [Hackaday.io](https://hackaday.io/projects), repair and disassembly through [iFixit](https://www.ifixit.com/), open recycling systems through [Precious Plastic](https://www.preciousplastic.com/about/open-source), and circular-design principles through the [Ellen MacArthur Foundation](https://www.ellenmacarthurfoundation.org/topics/circular-design/overview). The [full free-resource directory · Work in Progress](../resources/work-in-progress/index.qmd) groups provisional tools and references by fabrication task and explains what must be checked before reuse.

::: {.ter-curriculum-relevance}
**Ontario curriculum relevance:** Connections may include **TMJ**, **TDJ**, **TCJ**, **TTJ**, **TGJ**, and **TIJ1O**, depending on the process, project, and evidence. Course codes identify useful contexts, not one-to-one expectation mappings.
:::
